html:
The siege of Port Arthur lasted from August 1904 to 2 January 1905. Port Arthur, now Lüshunkou in China, was a Russian naval base at the southern tip of Manchuria. The Japanese army took it after five months.

Japan had won the port from China in 1895, but Russia, France and Germany forced it to hand the port back. Russia then leased it for its own Pacific fleet. The Russo-Japanese War began in February 1904 with a surprise Japanese attack on the ships there. General Nogi Maresuke's army closed in by land. His massed attacks on forts, trenches, barbed wire and machine guns failed with terrible losses. In December the Japanese took 203 Metre Hill, which looked over the harbour, and their heavy guns sank the Russian ships. The garrison then surrendered. Japan had about 58,000 killed and wounded, Russia about 31,000.

The fall of the fortress shocked Russia and helped set off the revolution of 1905. It freed Nogi's army for the Battle of Mukden, and it left the Russian Baltic fleet, then sailing east, with no base to go to; see the Battle of Tsushima. The trench fighting was a preview of World War I.
